deviation.title: Keep briefing exception names and suppress N818 with noqa
deviation.decision: Ruff requires an `Error` suffix, but the briefing fixes the names `InvalidUrl` and `CodeCollision`. The agent kept the names and added a per-line `# noqa: N818` rather than renaming them or changing the ruff config.

task.title: URL validation, code generation and link storage
task.spec:
In src/shortlink/links.py (no fastapi import):
- `class InvalidUrl(ValueError)` and `class CodeCollision(RuntimeError)`.
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class Link: code: str; url: str; created_at: str`.
- `validate_url(url: str) -> str`: raise InvalidUrl if url is empty, longer than 2048 characters, contains any character with ord < 0x20, ord == 0x7f, or for which str.isspace() is true; then urllib.parse.urlsplit: scheme (lowercased) must be http or https, hostname must be non-empty, username and password must be None, and accessing .port must not raise ValueError (else InvalidUrl). Non-ASCII characters elsewhere are accepted. Returns the url unchanged.
- CODE_ALPHABET = string.ascii_letters + string.digits; CODE_LENGTH = 6; `generate_code() -> str` uses secrets.choice; `is_valid_code(code: str) -> bool` checks length 6 and all characters in the alphabet.
- `create_link(conn, url, gen: Callable[[], str] = generate_code) -> Link`: validates the url, created_at = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"), tries up to 5 times to INSERT (parameterised) with a fresh gen() code, catching sqlite3.IntegrityError on the primary key and retrying; commits on success; after 5 collisions raises CodeCollision.
- `get_link(conn, code) -> Link | None`: returns None without querying when not is_valid_code(code); otherwise one parameterised SELECT.
Tests in tests/test_links.py (unit, using db.connect on the db_file fixture path).
acceptance: validate_url accepts http://example.com, https://example.com/a?b=1#c, HTTPS://EXAMPLE.COM, http://localhost:8000/x and https://example.com/café (tests)

validate_url raises InvalidUrl for: empty string, ftp://example.com, javascript:alert(1), http:// (no host), example.com (no scheme), https://user:[REDACTED:EMAIL], a URL with a space, with \n, with \t, with \x00, with \x7f, http://example.com:99999, and a 2049-character URL; a 2048-character URL is accepted (tests, parametrised)
generate_code returns 6 characters from CODE_ALPHABET (test)
create_link with a gen that always returns the same code: the first call succeeds, the second raises CodeCollision after 5 attempts (test)
create_link with a gen returning a taken code once then a free one succeeds (test)
get_link returns None for an unknown valid code and for malformed codes like 'abc', 'abc!de', '' (tests)
shortlink.links imports neither fastapi nor shortlink.stats (lint-imports passes)
all gates pass

plan.goal: API clients can POST a valid http(s) URL to /links and get a 6-character code, and GET /{code} redirects (302) to the original URL. The repo also gets the tooling every existing gate needs (mypy strict, import-linter contracts, pytest-cov, stricter ruff incl. bandit rules, pip-audit), so the gates actually judge the work.
out_of_scope: auth, custom aliases, expiration, edit/delete, rate limiting
deduplication: the same URL gets a new code each time
blocking internal hosts (localhost, private IPs): the service never fetches the URL, so there is no SSRF; the redirect only sends the user's own browser there
click counting and stats (feature click-stats)
a full short URL in the response (only the code is returned)

review.issue: create_link catches every sqlite3.IntegrityError and retries, but the task says to catch the primary-key collision. Any other integrity failure (e.g. a NOT NULL or CHECK violation) would be retried five times and then reported as CodeCollision, which hides the real error. Narrowing the catch to the primary-key case, for example by checking the error message or by using INSERT OR IGNORE and checking rowcount, would match the spec.

deviation.title: Wrap non-conflict IntegrityError in LinkStorageError instead of re-raising
deviation.decision: The briefing said to re-raise, but the convention says repositories must not leak SQLAlchemy exceptions. The class lives in application/errors.py because the application layer cannot import persistence. The original error is chained as the cause. The agent told the user it can be reverted.

task.title: Persistence: SQLite link repository
task.spec:
src/shortlink/persistence/db.py: SQLAlchemy 2 typed declarative `Base`; `def make_engine(database_url: str) -> Engine` (for sqlite URLs pass connect_args={"check_same_thread": False, "timeout": 30}); `def create_schema(engine: Engine) -> None` (Base.metadata.create_all); `def make_session_factory(engine) -> sessionmaker[Session]`.

src/shortlink/persistence/models.py: `LinkRow` table `links`: id Integer primary key autoincrement; code String(7) not null unique (UniqueConstraint named uq_links_code); url Text not null; created_at DateTime(timezone=True) not null.

src/shortlink/persistence/repository.py: `class SqlLinkRepository` implementing the LinkRepository port, constructed with a sessionmaker. add: insert in its own transaction; IntegrityError on uq_links_code -> raise CodeConflictError (from the IntegrityError); any other IntegrityError re-raised. get_by_code: select by code, map to domain Link; SQLite returns naive datetimes, so mapping sets tzinfo=UTC when missing. No SQLAlchemy type or exception leaves this module except through the port.

Tests in tests/persistence/test_repository.py using a tmp_path file database (sqlite:///{tmp_path}/t.db).
acceptance: Test: add then get_by_code returns an equal Link, created_at timezone-aware UTC
Test: get_by_code of an unknown code returns None
Test: adding a second link with the same code raises CodeConflictError and the first link is unchanged
Test: a URL with unicode and a 2048-char URL round-trip unchanged
Test: inserting a row with NULL url directly via the session fails (constraint is real)
lint-imports keeps 'layers' (persistence does not import api); all gates pass

plan.goal: A JSON API where POST /links stores a validated http/https URL under a random 7-char base62 code, and GET /{code} answers 302 to it. Also sets up the project tooling and the quality gates (ruff format, ruff lint, mypy strict, import-linter layer contracts, pytest with coverage) that every later task is judged by.
out_of_scope: authentication or users
custom aliases
link expiration
editing or deleting links
rate limiting
any frontend
deduplicating the same URL (every POST creates a new code)
DNS resolution of target hosts (only literal hosts/IPs are checked)
database migrations tool (tables come from metadata.create_all)
click counting (feature click-stats)

review.issue: _CODE_CONFLICT_MARKERS uses the substring 'links.code', so any IntegrityError on links.code is mapped to CodeConflictError, including SQLite's 'NOT NULL constraint failed: links.code'. The briefing says only uq_links_code maps to a conflict and other IntegrityErrors are re-raised. A NULL code would be reported as a code conflict. The domain always sets code, so this is hard to reach, but the match is looser than the spec. Fix: match on 'UNIQUE constraint failed: links.code' (and 'uq_links_code') instead, and add a test for a NULL code via the repository path.

deviation.title: Keep ValueError for naive datetime in record_click instead of mapping it to an HTTP error
deviation.decision: The only trigger is an injected clock returning a naive datetime, which is a wiring bug. The default `utc_now` is timezone-aware. Mapping it to 404/503 would hide the bug. The plan asks for the `ValueError`, a test asserts it, and `add` already has the same check. The agent suggested validating the clock output in `LinkService` if a guard is wanted. The reviewer's finding was marked blocking while its text said advisory, and the agent did not resolve it.

task.title: Count on redirect and GET /links/{code}/stats
task.spec:
Application (src/shortlink/application/links.py):
- resolve(code): after the malformed-code check and get_by_code, call repository.record_click(code, clock()); if it returns False raise LinkNotFoundError; return the link.
- new `stats(self, code: str) -> Link`: malformed code -> LinkNotFoundError without touching the repository; get_by_code None -> LinkNotFoundError; never records a click.

API: schemas.py `StatsResponse(code: str, url: str, clicks: int, created_at: datetime, last_clicked_at: datetime | None)`. routes.py: GET /links/{code}/stats, response_model StatsResponse, LinkNotFoundError -> HTTPException(404, detail="link not found"). GET /{code} keeps 302 and 404 behaviour unchanged.

README.md: document GET /links/{code}/stats with a curl example, that only successful redirects count, and that no visitor data is stored.

Tests: tests/application/test_links.py (fixed clock) and tests/api/test_stats_api.py (TestClient, follow_redirects=False).
acceptance: Test: a fresh link's stats -> 200 with clicks 0 and last_clicked_at null
Test: after 3 GET /{code} redirects, stats shows clicks 3 and last_clicked_at set (application test checks it equals the clock time)
Test: calling stats repeatedly does not change clicks
Test: GET /{code} for an unknown or malformed code -> 404 and no click is recorded anywhere
Test: stats for an unknown valid code and a malformed code ('abc') -> 404 {"detail": "link not found"}
Test: clicks on one link do not change another link's stats
Response body has exactly the keys code, url, clicks, created_at, last_clicked_at (no visitor data)
All gates pass

plan.goal: Every successful GET /{code} redirect increments the link's click counter atomically and records the time; GET /links/{code}/stats returns code, url, clicks, created_at and last_clicked_at.
out_of_scope: storing IP, user-agent, referrer or any per-visitor data
per-day or time-series stats
unique-visitor counting or bot filtering
migrations for existing databases
counting HEAD requests or failed redirects
authentication on the stats endpoint

review.issue: link_stats maps LinkStorageError to STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, which reads "could not store the link, try again". This is a read failure, and the README's new stats section says 503 means "the link could not be read; try again". The test test_storage_failure_on_stats_is_503_with_string_detail asserts the same wrong "could not store" text, so it locks the mismatch in. Fix: give stats its own detail (e.g. "could not read the link, try again") or make the README match, and update the test.

task.title: Domain: Link, URL validation and code generation
task.spec:
Pure domain rules for links, stdlib only.

**Where**
- `src/shortlink/domain/links.py`
- `tests/domain/__init__.py`, `tests/domain/test_links.py`

**How**
- `Link`: frozen dataclass `code: str`, `url: str`, `created_at: datetime` (no click fields)
- `InvalidUrlError(Exception)` with a `reason: str` attribute
- `ALPHABET = digits + ascii_lowercase + ascii_uppercase`, `CODE_LENGTH = 7`, `MAX_URL_LENGTH = 2048`
- `generate_code() -> str` with `secrets.choice`; `is_valid_code(value: str) -> bool`
- `validate_target_url(raw: str) -> str`, checks in this order, each with its reason: empty → `"url is required"`; > 2048 → `"url is too long"`; any char < 0x20, 0x7F or whitespace → `"url contains control or whitespace characters"`; scheme not http/https (case-insensitive) → `"only http and https urls are allowed"`; no host → `"url must have a host"`; user or password → `"urls with credentials are not allowed"`; bad port → `"invalid port"`; internal host → `"internal hosts are not allowed"`
- internal host: `localhost`, `*.localhost` (trailing dot ignored), any IP literal that is not `is_global` (IPv4 and bracketed IPv6), and numeric/hex IPv4 forms that `ipaddress` rejects (`2130706433`, `0x7f.1`, `127.1`)
- returns the URL unchanged
acceptance: test: generate_code returns 7 chars from ALPHABET; 1000 calls give > 990 distinct codes
test: is_valid_code rejects 6 and 8 chars, `-`, `_` and non-ASCII letters
test: accepts `http://example.com`, `HTTPS://Example.com/a?b=1#c`, an IDN host `https://bücher.example`, a URL of exactly 2048 chars

test: rejects empty, 2049 chars, `\n`, `\t`, a space, `\x7f`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `ftp://x.com`, `mailto:[REDACTED:EMAIL]`, `http://`, `http://user:[REDACTED:EMAIL]`, `http://x.com:99999`, each with its reason
domain/links.py imports only the standard library (pure domain contract)

DNS resolution of hosts

task.title: Domain and application: LinkStats and StatsService
task.spec:
Stats types and the use case that combines a link with its click totals.

**Where**
- `src/shortlink/domain/stats.py`
- `src/shortlink/application/stats.py`
- `tests/domain/test_stats.py`, `tests/application/test_stats.py`

**How**
- domain: frozen dataclasses `ClickTotals(clicks: int, last_clicked_at: datetime)` and `LinkStats(code, url, clicks: int, created_at: datetime, last_clicked_at: datetime | None)`
- application: `ClickStore` (Protocol) with `record(code: str, at: datetime) -> None` and `totals(code: str) -> ClickTotals | None`; both raise `LinkStorageError` (from `shortlink.application.links`) on failure
- `StatsService(links: LinkService, store: ClickStore)`, `stats(code) -> LinkStats`: `links.get(code)` (LinkNotFoundError propagates), then `store.totals(code)`; none → `clicks = 0`, `last_clicked_at = None`
- stats never calls `LinkService.resolve` (reading stats is not a click)
acceptance: test (fake store, fake link repository): a link with no clicks → clicks 0, last_clicked_at None
test: a link with totals (3, t) → clicks 3, last_clicked_at t, url and created_at from the link
test: unknown or malformed code raises LinkNotFoundError and the store is not read
test: stats() records no click
no file `shortlink/*/links.py` changes in this task

per-click history (no row per click, no referrer, user agent or IP)
